proofs.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: an explicit diagonal schedule over the safe shared-trace finite classes.}

Let \(A_{\mathfrak G}\) be the computable integer supplied by
\(\mathrm{lem:shared\mbox{-}extension\mbox{-}coverage\mbox{-}risk}\).  The validated finite encoding of \(\mathfrak G\) permits exact comparison with its strictly positive honesty level \(\eta\).  Therefore the search
\[
 j_0=\min\left\{j\ge2:
 j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G},\quad
 \frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}+\frac1j<1\right\}
\tag{30}
\]
terminates.  For \(m\in\mathbb N\), put
\[
 j(m)=j_0+m+1,
 \qquad
 \Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)
 =\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j(m)^2}+\frac1{j(m)}.
\tag{31}
\]
This is a positive rational number computed from the input, it decreases with \(m\), and it converges to zero.

Run the finite construction in the shared-extension lemma at level \(j(m)\), and mix every enumerated rational vertex rule globally with the full-set action using probability \(1/j(m)\).  Call the resulting finite rational class \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\).  Its geometry is computed by
\(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) on the explicit common fan \(\operatorname{recFan}(\mathfrak G)\).  Take the maximum of the finitely many chart thresholds and collar endpoints as the one common rational core radius.  The construction in
\(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) supplies the rational partitions, the global common-face mesh, all incidence maps, and the retained component-to-semantic-label projections.  Every step is a finite enumeration of rational active sets, cones, simplices, probability grids, or outward rational error allocations, so this is an algorithm from \((\mathfrak G,m)\).

Now fix \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\).  The existential nearest rational assignment in the shared-extension lemma gives \(Q_{j(m)}\) in the unrepaired finite class.  Since \(j(m)\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), its rational full-set mixture \(\widetilde K_m=Q_{j(m)}^{\mathrm{rep}}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,m}\).  Equation (28) gives the stronger conclusion
\[
 \inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}
 P_h\{v\in\widetilde K_m(W)\}\ge1-\eta.
\tag{32}
\]
Equation (29) and (31) give
\[
 R_r(\widetilde K_m)
 \le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m),
\tag{33}
\]
and the repaired ledger conclusion of that lemma gives
\[
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}(\widetilde K_m)
 \le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(m)<1.
\tag{34}
\]
The path part of (34) is legitimate even at seam-centered means by
\(\mathrm{lem:slow\mbox{-}collar\mbox{-}ledger}\) and the declared weighted-gluing inequality; it does not identify independently averaged face and cone rules.  The cone-interior products are path-independent by the declared common-ray coherence lemma, while their statistical validity follows separately from the safe-sector inclusions and (22).  Thus (32)--(34) establish every assertion in the target theorem, with the explicit input-dependent modulus (31).

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and every rational \(\tau\in(0,1)\), finite rational active-set analysis computes a rational number \(R_0(\tau)\), a finite barycentrically subdivided rational recession cover \(\{U_\alpha\}_{\alpha\in\mathcal S_\tau}\), rational safe cones \(C_\alpha\), bounded normal bases \(B_\alpha\subset N_\alpha\), affine sections \(\varsigma_\alpha:B_\alpha\to\mathbb R^d\) whose linear parts are the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-orthogonal lifts of the quotient coordinates, and protected stars with the following properties.  The core \(\{h:\|h\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}\le R_0(\tau)\}\) together with the \(U_\alpha\)'s covers \(\mathbb R^d\).  If \(h\in U_\alpha\), \(n=\pi_\alpha h\), and \(v\in\mathcal V(h)\), then
\[
 \varsigma_\alpha(n)+C_\alpha\subseteq D_v.
\]
If in addition \(h\in H_r\), then
\[
 \varsigma_\alpha(n)+C_\alpha\subseteq H_r.
\]
These inclusions hold simultaneously for every chart in the protected star of \(h\).  A change of component, projection active set, or unique-label status is either assigned to a lower-dimensional member of the same barycentric incidence diagram or is separated from the protected star by an explicitly computed Mahalanobis distance.  All constants, incidence maps, semantic projections, distances, and the number \(R_0(\tau)\) are obtained by terminating rational linear algebra, rational linear feasibility, and outward rational bounds for finitely many positive quadratic forms.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: finite projection active sets followed by a kernel-stratified recession decomposition.}

Write the finite component list as \(P_i=\{x:A_i x\le b_i\}\), retaining the map from \(i\) to its semantic label.  Fix one component \(P_i\) and a linearly independent subset \(I\) of its rows.  Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\), from \(\mathrm{ass:rational\mbox{-}positive\mbox{-}covariance}\), implies that
\[
 G_{iI}=A_{iI}\Sigma A_{iI}^{\prime}
\]
is positive definite.  Hence the following objects are rational and computable:
\[
 \lambda_{iI}(x)=G_{iI}^{-1}(A_{iI}x-b_{iI}),\qquad
 \Pi_{iI}(x)=x-\Sigma A_{iI}^{\prime}\lambda_{iI}(x),
\tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 e_{iI}(x)=x-\Pi_{iI}(x)=M_{iI}x+c_{iI},\qquad
 M_{iI}=\Sigma A_{iI}^{\prime}G_{iI}^{-1}A_{iI}.
\tag{2}
\]
On the rational polyhedron
\[
 Q_{iI}=\{x:\lambda_{iI}(x)\ge0,\ A_i\Pi_{iI}(x)\le b_i\},
\tag{3}
\]
the point \(\Pi_{iI}(x)\) is the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-metric projection of \(x\) on \(P_i\).  Indeed, for \(g\in P_i\), (1) gives
\[
 \langle x-\Pi_{iI}(x),g-\Pi_{iI}(x)\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}
 =\lambda_{iI}(x)^{\prime}A_{iI}\{g-\Pi_{iI}(x)\}\le0.
\tag{4}
\]
Expanding the squared norm and using (4) shows
\(\|x-g\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}^2\ge
\|x-\Pi_{iI}(x)\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}^2\).  Conversely, the projection optimality inequality has a nonnegative normal multiplier; deleting redundant active normals leaves one of the finitely many linearly independent sets \(I\).  Thus the sets in (3) cover \(\mathbb R^d\), with harmless overlap on active-set boundaries, and on \(Q_{iI}\)
\[
 d_i(x)^2:=\operatorname{dist}_{\Sigma^{-1}}(x,P_i)^2
 =(A_{iI}x-b_{iI})^{\prime}G_{iI}^{-1}(A_{iI}x-b_{iI}).
\tag{5}
\]

The linear map \(M_{iI}\) is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite for the \(\Sigma^{-1}\) inner product, and
\[
 \langle M_{iI}y,z\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}
 =(A_{iI}y)^{\prime}G_{iI}^{-1}(A_{iI}z),
 \qquad
 \ker M_{iI}=\ker A_{iI}.
\tag{6}
\]
Moreover \(c_{iI}\) lies in the range of \(M_{iI}\).  Equations (5)--(6) are the promised finite projection systems.  In particular, the completed label profile and membership in \(H_r\) are decided by a finite Boolean combination of rational linear inequalities and inequalities of the form \(d_i(x)^2\ge r^2\).

We next construct the tail sectors.  For every tuple \(J\) containing one component for each label incident at a point, exact rational feasibility computes
\[
 P_J=\bigcap_{i\in J}P_i,qquad
 C_J=\operatorname{rec}(P_J)=\{y:A_i y\le0\text{ for all }i\in J\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Enumerating feasible row bases computes the vertices modulo lineality and the primitive rational extreme rays of \(C_J\).  Thus
\[
 P_J=Q_J+C_J
\tag{8}
\]
for a computable bounded rational polytope \(Q_J\) in a rational complement of the lineality space.  If \(C_J=\{0\}\), (8) is bounded; taking the maximum of its finitely many vertex norms places the whole cell in the core.  Consequently every point outside a computable preliminary core that has profile \(J\) has a nonzero recession representation.

Refine each \(C_J\) simultaneously by the common fan \(\operatorname{recFan}(\mathfrak G)\), by all rational subspaces \(\ker M_{iI}\), and then simplicially.  On a projective slice of a pointed cone, use rational simplicial subdivisions of diameter at most \(\tau\).  The following finite recursion removes the only possible lack of a uniform positive margin.  On a face \(F\), first assign a neighborhood of every nonzero cone
\[
 F\cap\bigcap_{(i,I)\in E}\ker M_{iI}
\tag{9}
\]
to its lower-dimensional barycentric star.  Its rays lie literally in every kernel in \(E\).  On the closed remainder, compactness of the rational projective slice and (6) give, for every remaining pair \((i,I)\), a strictly positive minimum of
\[
 (A_{iI}y)^{\prime}G_{iI}^{-1}(A_{iI}\varrho)
\tag{10}
\]
when \(y\) is in the sector and \(\varrho\) is one of its sufficiently close rational generators.  A terminating rational interval subdivision finds a positive rational lower bound \(\gamma\) for (10): if no such lower bound exists, a nested sequence of rational boxes has a limit in the kernel and was already assigned by (9).  This is a finite induction because each passage to (9) lowers dimension or enlarges the set \(E\).

For \(h=x+t y\), with \(x\) in the bounded base from (8), a selected sector ray \(\varrho\) therefore satisfies either \(M_{iI}\varrho=0\), in which case
\[
 \langle e_{iI}(h),\varrho\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}=0,
\tag{11}
\]
or
\[
 \langle e_{iI}(h),\varrho\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}
 =t\langle M_{iI}y,\varrho\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}
   +\langle M_{iI}x+c_{iI},\varrho\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}
 \ge t\gamma-C_{iI,J}.
\tag{12}
\]
The constants \(C_{iI,J}\) are maximized on finitely many bounded rational bases and enclosed outward by rationals.  Taking
\[
 R_0(\tau)\ge
 \max_{i,I,J}\frac{C_{iI,J}}{\gamma_{iI,J,\tau}}
\tag{13}
\]
after conversion from recession coefficients to Mahalanobis norm makes every expression in (12) nonnegative.  Degenerate lineality directions are represented by their two primitive orientations and obey (11).

To see why (11)--(13) are exactly the required safety certificate, let \(z\) be any nonnegative combination of the rays in a chart star.  By (7), \(z\in\operatorname{rec}(P_i)\) for every component representing an incident semantic label, so
\[
 h\in P_i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad h+z\in P_i.
\tag{14}
\]
For a competing component \(P_i\), the function \(x\mapsto d_i(x)^2/2\) is convex and differentiable, with directional derivative
\(\langle e_i(x),z\rangle_{\Sigma^{-1}}\).  The active-set formula at \(h\), together with (11)--(12), gives a nonnegative derivative.  Convexity consequently yields
\[
 d_i(h+z)^2\ge d_i(h)^2
 \quad\text{for every competing component }P_i.
\tag{15}
\]
Taking the minimum over the finitely many components of each \(D_u\) proves that positive separation cannot decrease.  If \(r=0\), uniqueness still gives \(d_i(h)>0\) because each competing \(D_u\) is closed; (15) preserves this strict positivity.  Hence (14)--(15) preserve \(H_r\), including its unique-label requirement.

Finally, sort the finitely many recession coefficients in (8) into scale blocks.  Comparable coefficients form one simplicial cone chart; a ratio exceeding the prescribed rational collar scale creates a face inclusion and the construction recurses on the lower block.  There are at most \(d\) nonzero blocks.  On a fixed projection cell, substitution of \(x+t y\) into (5) gives
\[
 d_i(x+t y)^2=a_{iI}(x,y)t^2+2b_{iI}(x,y)t+c_{iI}(x),
 \qquad a_{iI}(x,y)\ge0.
\tag{16}
\]
After the derivative threshold (13), this polynomial is nondecreasing.  If an associated tail cell meets \(H_r\), then either \(a_{iI}>0\), in which case the larger root of the rational quadratic inequality in (16) is enclosed above by a terminating rational bisection, or \(a_{iI}=0\), in which case (11) makes the distance constant and its value is already at least \(r\).  Maximizing these finitely many root bounds over the bounded normal base produces an outward rational threshold at which all competing distances are at least \(r\).  Cells for which the inequality never holds contribute no point of \(H_r\) and are omitted from the risk subcover.

Choose the complement in (8) to be the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-orthogonal complement of the current tangential span.  Replacing the first coefficient in each scale block by a single rational number larger than the maxima of (13) and the root bounds, uniformly over the bounded normal base, gives
\[
 \varsigma_\alpha(n)=S_\alpha n+c_\alpha,
\tag{17}
\]
where \(S_\alpha\) is the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-orthogonal lift and \(c_\alpha\) is a fixed rational safe recession vector.  This uniform choice is possible precisely because the normal base is bounded and every non-kernel quadratic margin has the positive lower bound computed in (10).  All residual normal coordinates range over a computable bounded polytope \(B_\alpha\).  Equations (14)--(16) hold on the whole nonnegative box based at that section, proving both the label and \(H_r\) inclusions rather than merely their forward invariance from the original point.  Component changes are faces of (7), projection changes are faces of (3), and zero margins in (10) were assigned in (9).  Closing under faces and taking the barycentric subdivision therefore covers every boundary with its completed incident labels.  Rational linear programming computes distances between disjoint closed stars; zero distance triggers another shared face, while positive distance is enclosed below by a rational.  This supplies the protected stars and proves every assertion of the lemma by a finite, input-computable construction.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the inductive shared-trace extension there is an input-computable integer \(C_{\mathfrak G}\ge1\) such that, for rational \(L,B\ge1\), the rational cutoffs, the subordinate partition of unity, the incidence forest, and protected neighborhoods can be chosen so that all chart traces agree exactly on simultaneous supports and, for every \(f:\mathcal A\to[0,R_f]\),
\[
 \sum_{\tau\prec\sigma}\int
 \|\nabla\chi_{\tau\sigma}(w)\|_{\Sigma}
 |F_\sigma^f(w)-F_\tau^f(w)|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}R_f}{L},
\]
and, on every declared coverage or separated-risk mean cell,
\[
 \sum_e\Gamma_{C,e}^f+\frac{R_f}{2}\omega(h)
 \le C_{\mathfrak G}R_f
 \left(\frac{d}{L}+\frac{d}{B^2}\right).
\]
Both inequalities are uniform in \(h\), including means centered on an incidence seam, and do not require the incident cone-interior candidates to be close.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: exact trace induction plus slow-cutoff variation, rather than convergence of independently averaged charts.}

On a rational collar coordinate \(a\), begin with the piecewise-linear cutoff
\[
 \chi_L(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&a\le0,\\
 a/L,&0<a<L,\\
 1,&a\ge L.
 \end{cases}
\tag{16}
\]
If the dual Mahalanobis norm of the rational collar coordinate is \(c_a\), replace the physical collar length by \(c_aL\).  Then \(\|\nabla\chi_L\|_\Sigma\le L^{-1}\).  The barycentric subdivision has a computable overlap number and every incidence path has length at most its finite dimension.  Let \(C_{\mathfrak G}\) dominate the sum of these finitely many overlap and path constants.

Because \(0\le F_\alpha^f\le R_f\),
\[
 \int \|\nabla\chi_{\tau\sigma}(w)\|_\Sigma
 |F_\sigma^f(w)-F_\tau^f(w)|\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,dw
 \le \frac{R_f}{L}.
\tag{17}
\]
Summing (17) over the bounded number of active collars proves the first displayed inequality.  Notice that only boundedness was used; the endpoint discrepancy may equal \(R_f\).

The dimension induction in \(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) copies, rather than recomputes, a lower-skeleton rule.  Thus two incident chart restrictions are identical wherever their partition weights are simultaneously positive.  This remains true at a branching intersection because the induction has a single already-constructed value there.  For a mean cell \(C\), choose as anchor its deepest active stratum and route every other active chart along the barycentric parent path.  Take \(P_{C,e}\) to contain the guarded star on which the two endpoint restrictions are identical.  On this set the first integrand in \(\Gamma_{C,e}^f\) is zero whenever the corresponding path load is locally active.

The remaining path load has one of two causes.  Either its chart has zero weight at \(h\), or the observation crossed the guard of width \(B\).  In the first case it is bounded by the total weight variation.  Since the sum of the dual Mahalanobis Lipschitz constants of the partition is at most \(C_{\mathfrak G}/L\), writing \(W=h+\Sigma^{1/2}Z\), with \(Z\sim N_d(0,I_d)\), gives
\[
 \omega(h)
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}}{L}E\|Z\|_2
 \le \frac{C_{\mathfrak G}d}{L}.
\tag{18}
\]
In the second case, Markov's inequality applied to \(\|Z\|_2^2\), whose expectation is \(d\), gives
\[
 P_h\{\|W-h\|_{\Sigma^{-1}}>B\}
 \le \frac{d}{B^2}.
\tag{19}
\]
Multiplying (18)--(19) by \(R_f\), and then by the computably bounded path multiplicity, bounds both the protected-set integral and the complement term in every \(\Gamma_{C,e}^f\).  Enlarging \(C_{\mathfrak G}\) once proves the second displayed inequality.  Exact traces, not a small endpoint difference, cover seam-centered means.  This proves the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement:
There is an input-computable integer \(A_{\mathfrak G}\ge1\) with the following property.  For every integer \(j\ge1\), the safe-sector geometry and inductive shared-trace construction determine a finite class \(\mathfrak H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of rational globally meshed rules, independently of \(K\), such that every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\) has a member \(Q_j\in\mathfrak H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}P_h\{v\in Q_j(W)\}
 \ge1-\eta-\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2},
\]
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_r}E_h\ell\{Q_j(W)\}
 \le R_r(K)+D\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}(Q_j)\le\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}.
\]
If \(j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), the rational global mixture
\[
 Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}}=(1-j^{-1})Q_j+j^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{V\}}
\]
has coverage at least \(1-\eta\), risk at most
\[
 R_r(K)+D\left(\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}+\frac1j\right),
\]
and total repaired ledger at most \(A_{\mathfrak G}/j^2+1/j\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: covariance-orthogonal safe averaging, slowly varying convex gluing, and exhaustive rational finite elements.}

Fix \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\) and \(s>0\).  For the coverage functional
\(f_v(A)=\mathbf 1\{v\in A\}\), the honesty of \(K\) and
\(\mathrm{lem:gaussian\mbox{-}smoothing}\) give, for \(h\in D_v\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_s}^{f_v}(W)\ge1-\eta-\epsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \epsilon_s=\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}.
\tag{20}
\]
For \(f=\ell\), the same lemma gives, for \(h\in H_r\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_s}^{\ell}(W)\le R_r(K)+D\epsilon_s.
\tag{21}
\]

Consider an outer chart \(\alpha\).  In whitened coordinates the normal and tangential Gaussian components in
\(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) are independent.  Fubini's theorem therefore gives, for every bounded action functional \(f\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_\alpha^\circ}^{f}(W)
 =\frac1{|H_{\alpha,L}|}
 \int_{H_{\alpha,L}}
 E_{\varsigma_\alpha(\pi_\alpha h)+t}
 F_{q_s}^{f}(W)\,dt.
\tag{22}
\]
If \(h\in D_v\) and chart \(\alpha\) is active at \(h\), the first inclusion in
\(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) puts every mean on the right of (22) in \(D_v\).  If \(h\in H_r\), its second inclusion puts every such mean in \(H_r\).  Hence (20)--(22) prove the same coverage and risk bounds for every chart candidate active at \(h\).  On a completed equality face this argument applies to every incident label; no boundary label is discarded.  The product representation and incidence-path independence of the box average are exactly those proved in \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\).  The finite tangential approximation error, when the conditional Gaussian average in (22) is replaced by a finite chart average, is bounded by \(\mathrm{lem:single\mbox{-}chart\mbox{-}averaging}\) and is charged below.

Let \(\{\mu_a\}\) denote all the core, incidence, and internal collar weights used by the extension.  At each point they are nonnegative and sum to one.  For any \([0,R_f]\)-valued functional,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_hF_{\widehat q}^{f}(W)
 &=\sum_a\mu_a(h)E_hF_{q_a}^{f}(W)\\
 &\quad+E_h\sum_a\{\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)\}F_{q_a}^{f}(W).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
The coefficients in the last sum add to zero.  The range bound therefore implies
\[
 \left|E_h\sum_a\{\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)\}F_{q_a}^{f}(W)\right|
 \le\frac{R_f}{2}E_h\sum_a|\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)|.
\tag{24}
\]
Every term with \(\mu_a(h)>0\) is safe by (20)--(22); terms with zero mean weight enter only the remainder (24).  The slow-collar lemma bounds (24), uniformly in \(h\), by \(C_{\mathfrak G}R_fd/(2L)\).  Its second inequality and the established weighted-gluing inequality simultaneously bound the complete path ledger.  Thus data-dependent chart selection introduces no uncharged boundary-honesty or risk step.

It remains to make the rule finite and rational.  The core is bounded.  Every outer candidate is a function only of its bounded normal base \(B_\alpha\); all unbounded tangential coordinates were integrated out in (22).  Gaussian smoothing gives the global \(\ell_1\)-Lipschitz bound \(s^{-1}\sqrt{2/\pi}\), and averaging is a contraction.  The only additional derivative is the cutoff derivative bounded in (17).  The exact rational geometry therefore computes an outward rational Lipschitz constant \(H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) on every bounded chart.  Triangulate all normal bases on one rational mesh of diameter at most
\[
 \delta_j\le \frac{1}{j^2H_{\mathfrak G,j}},
\tag{25}
\]
using one vertex on each common face.  At every vertex, approximate the action-probability vector by a rational simplex vector within \(j^{-2}\) after allocating this tolerance over the finite vertices.  Affine interpolation stays in the probability simplex and, by (25), changes every \([0,R_f]\)-expectation by at most a computable multiple of \(R_fj^{-2}\).  Enumerating all rational simplex assignments at that denominator produces a finite class independent of \(K\), and the simultaneous nearest assignment to the candidates constructed from this particular \(K\) is one member of it.  Shared vertices are rounded once, so exact traces survive rationalization.

Choose
\[
 s_j=j^{-1},\qquad L_j=j^2,\qquad B_j=j,
\tag{26}
\]
use recession refinement parameter \(j^{-1}\), and allocate at most \(j^{-2}\) in total to tangential averaging, finite elements, Gaussian integration, covariance enclosures, and rational rounding.  The smoothing term obeys \(\epsilon_{s_j}\le d/j^2\).  Equations (18)--(19), (25), and the finite allocation just described show that a computable integer \(A_{\mathfrak G}\) can be chosen to dominate, after normalization of the risk entries by the positive number \(D\), every chart, seam, protected-neighborhood, tail, covariance, integration, and rounding charge:
\[
 e_j\le \frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}.
\tag{27}
\]
The safe-sector threshold \(R_0(j^{-1})\) and the physical collar lengths may grow arbitrarily fast with \(j\); they are finite computable geometry outputs and do not alter (27).  This proves all three unrepaired inequalities in the statement.

Finally suppose \(j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), put \(\alpha=j^{-1}\), and mix with the deterministic full-set action.  From (27),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_h\{v\in Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}}(W)\}
 &\ge(1-\alpha)(1-\eta-e_j)+\alpha\\
 &=1-\eta-e_j+\alpha(\eta+e_j)\\
 &\ge1-\eta,
 \end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
because \(\alpha\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}/j^2\ge e_j\).  Since \(0\le R_r(K)\) and \(\ell(V)\le D\),
\[
 R_r(Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}})
 \le(1-\alpha)\{R_r(K)+De_j\}+\alpha D
 \le R_r(K)+D(e_j+\alpha).
\tag{29}
\]
Charging the same global mixture probability in the ledger gives
\(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}(Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}})\le e_j+\alpha\).  Equations (27)--(29) prove the repaired conclusions.

proposed.name: Inductive exact shared-trace extension
proposed.construction:
Fix a safe-sector system produced by \(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) and put \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\).  For a sector \(\alpha\), decompose the whitened Gaussian coordinate into the \(\Sigma^{-1}\)-orthogonal spaces \(N_\alpha\oplus T_\alpha\), let \(Z_\alpha\) be the centered residual tangential Gaussian, and let \(H_{\alpha,L}\) be a rational box contained in the safe cone \(C_\alpha\).  Define the cone-interior candidate on the bounded normal base by
\[
 q_\alpha^\circ(n,A)=\frac{1}{|H_{\alpha,L}|}
 \int_{H_{\alpha,L}}E\!left[
 q_s\{\varsigma_\alpha(n)+t+Z_\alpha,A\}\right]dt,
 \qquad A\in\mathcal A.
\]
The box integral is the product of the literally shared one-ray averaging factors on every incident cone.  On the barycentric subdivision, construct \(\widehat q\) by induction in stratum dimension.  An already constructed lower-skeleton rule is extended constantly through the new normal collar; it is used unchanged on every branching intersection.  In the part of an incident cone belonging only to that cone, interpolate convexly between this extension and \(q_\alpha^\circ\) with rational piecewise-linear cutoffs whose Mahalanobis dual derivative is at most \(L^{-1}\).  Distinct collars are separated by a rational guard width \(B\).  A single global rational simplicial mesh is used on all bounded normal bases, and a vertex on a common face is one shared action-probability variable.  Thus every chart is the restriction of the same global Markov kernel \(\widehat q\), while the cone-interior candidate retains the common-ray F\o lner representation.
inputs: a safe-sector certificate and one ancestor \(q_s=K*\phi_{s^2\Sigma}\)

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires a single recursively constructed global rule whose lower-skeleton values are literally shared at every branching intersection; this definition names that construction without asserting its safety or ledger properties.
